clue.text: We didn't like this Tesla vehicle's storage space

blocks.note: the jeer an audience gives to something it did not enjoy
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the luggage space in their Tesla car.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker but is the scientific unit. BOOT is one of the eight corner entries, all meaning kick (see 4 down).
explanation.definitionFit: In British English the luggage compartment of a car is called this; Americans say trunk.

clue.text: Faces away from boor on carpet, unconscious

indicators.note: a word's face is its front, so taking faces away removes the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: a lout is a rude, boorish person
to carpet someone is to call them in and reprimand them

explanation.surface: Someone passed out face down on a rug after a run-in with a lout.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet is a verb here: to be carpeted is to be told off by the boss. LOUT and SCOLD each lose their first letter, leaving OUT COLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knocked out or flat out is the idiom for being completely senseless after a blow.

clue.text: 50% of scary conservative district

indicators.note: taking fifty per cent means keeping half a word and dropping the other half

blocks.note: frightening; only its first half is kept
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A gloomy claim that half of a scary region is Conservative-voting.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRIFYING has ten letters, so 50% is its first five, TERRI. 'Conservative district' reads like a political phrase, but the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory is an area of land under one authority, much as a district is an administrative region.

clue.text: First in carvery, order unseasoned beef

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
plain food has no seasoning

explanation.surface: A diner at a carvery, a restaurant serving roast meats, orders the beef without seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef looks like the noun on the carvery menu, but it is a verb meaning grumble. COMPLAIN is a corner entry: to kick is to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is informal slang for to grumble or moan about something, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: My knickers in a twist seeing this grid's offensive entries?

definitions.note: the grid's corner entries are all synonyms of kick

indicators.note: something in a twist is contorted out of shape, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A prim solver gets flustered on spotting rude words in this crossword's answers.
explanation.walkthrough: To get your knickers in a twist is British slang for getting upset. The eight entries at this grid's corners (BOOT, COMPLAIN, GIVE UP, RECOIL, STRIKE, PUNGENCY, THRILL, TANG) can each mean kick, and offensive means attacking, as in football.
explanation.definitionFit: In football an awarded restart from the field's angle is an attacking set play, and here the grid's angles hold kick synonyms.

clue.text: Satisfied with opera in America

blocks.note: first meaning: fulfilled, as a requirement is
second meaning: the Metropolitan Opera in New York, known by its short name

explanation.surface: Someone content with an American opera production.
explanation.walkthrough: Satisfied is a past participle here, as in 'the conditions were satisfied'.
explanation.definitionFit: A demand that has been fulfilled has been met, and New York's Metropolitan Opera House is universally called the Met.

clue.text: One blooming bunch, crossworders

blocks.note: a lot is a group or set of people
the setter and solvers together: we crossworders

explanation.surface: Crossword fans are described as one flourishing gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Blooming looks like a mild British swear word, as in 'one blooming bunch', but here it means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant famous for its large flowers, so it is an example of something that blooms.

clue.text: In Byzantine rite, a reluctance to change?

indicators.note: something Byzantine is intricate and convoluted, so these letters are tangled up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Eastern Orthodox ritual is portrayed as resistant to change.
explanation.walkthrough: Byzantine looks like a description of the church rite, but it signals the letter shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency to keep doing what one already does, a resistance to any alteration.

clue.text: Soldier very quiet about EU surrender

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: GI is an American private soldier
v is the standard abbreviation of very
p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier says little about the European Union surrendering.
explanation.walkthrough: Very and quiet are the standard one-letter abbreviations, with p from music's piano. GIVE UP is a corner entry: to kick a habit is to give it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up is to yield or stop resisting, the phrasal-verb synonym of surrender.

clue.text: Quail ground to cook with head removed

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter, and removing it leaves the rest

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park for games
to boil is to cook in hot water; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A quail is minced before cooking, with its head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Quail is the bird in the surface but a verb in the answer, meaning flinch. RECOIL is a corner entry: a gun's kick is its recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, which is what one does when one flinches away.

clue.text: Explain Italian footballers opening British sandwich shop

indicators.note: to open something is to come at its start, so one piece goes first

blocks.note: Inter is Inter Milan, the Italian football club
Pret a Manger is a British chain of sandwich shops

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to explain why an Italian football team is launching a British sandwich outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as a shop launch, but it places the club before the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to make clear the meaning of something, a straight synonym of explain.

clue.text: Melody, not just any note

blocks.note: the definite article picks out one particular thing, not just any
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tune must be made of the right notes, not random ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just any' asks for the word that marks a specific thing rather than a general one.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the main tune of a piece of music, the melody on which it is built.

clue.text: Controversial drug and why one does it?

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a motive is the reason for doing something

explanation.surface: A divisive drug, and the question of why people take it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'why one does it' is a cryptic description of a word rather than a real question.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue arouses strong feelings and argument, so it is contentious in the same way.

clue.text: Gentleman returning extravagant duck dish

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the form of address for a gentleman
OTT is over the top, excessive
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A man goes back for a lavish duck dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck dish suggests a recipe, but duck is the cricket zero and the definition is only 'dish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice preparation cooked in stock, an example of a dish.

clue.text: Primitive Red Army unit out of position

indicators.note: things out of position are not where they should be, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crude Soviet military detachment has strayed from its post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primitive Red Army unit' reads as a description of soldiers; every letter of the last three words is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rudimentary is basic and undeveloped, at an early simple stage like a primitive thing.

clue.text: Secure lad freely admitted to having acne scars

indicators.note: done freely means done without constraint, so the letters move about at will
something admitted is let inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: skin pitted with scars is pocked
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-assured boy openly confesses to having pitted skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Secure looks like an adjective about the confident lad, but it means fastened, and 'freely admitted' splits into two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Padlocked means fastened with a detachable lock, so a padlocked door is secured shut.

clue.text: Write sloppily, erasing the initial stroke

indicators.note: rubbing out the initial means deleting the first letter of a word

blocks.note: to scrawl is to write untidily; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Messy handwriting rubs out the first pen stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroke looks like a pen mark, which fits the writing surface, but it is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The front crawl is the fastest swimming style, so it is an example of a stroke.

clue.text: Inexpert company invested in rude, slow server option?

indicators.note: money invested is put into something, so these pieces go inside another

blocks.note: lay means non-professional, without expert training
Co is the abbreviation for company
curt means abrupt to the point of rudeness

explanation.surface: A complaint about a rude, slow waiter from an amateurish firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The server is a tennis player serving, not a waiter or computer. LAYCO goes inside CURT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is played on several surfaces, and clay is the slow one where serves lose pace.

clue.text: Smart, perhaps, consuming volume after volume

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: say means for example, as perhaps does
V is the abbreviation for volume, written twice

explanation.surface: A clever person reads one book after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart, perhaps' looks like a definition by example, but perhaps is wordplay for SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Savvy means shrewd and knowledgeable, the informal equivalent of clever or sharp.

clue.text: Employees won’t work on this buffet

blocks.note: first meaning: a stoppage, when workers walk out
second meaning: to hit

explanation.surface: Staff refuse to serve at the buffet meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffet looks like the spread of food but is a verb, to strike or batter. STRIKE is a corner entry: to kick is to strike with the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers on a walkout are said to be on this, and the verb also means to hit or batter.

clue.text: Country transport working on connecting universities

indicators.note: something that connects two things sits between them, so one piece is placed in the middle

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle
U is the abbreviation for university, so two of them
to be at something is to be busy working on it

explanation.surface: A nation's transport system is being worked on to link its universities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working on' must be read together as AT, as in 'at it'; it is not the usual ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanuatu is an island nation in the South Pacific, an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Endlessly scour each match result

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly; it loses its last letter
ea is the abbreviation for each
a bout is a contest, as in boxing

explanation.surface: Someone pores over every game's final score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match result' looks like a scoreline, but result is a verb here meaning happen.
explanation.definitionFit: To come about is to happen or arise as a consequence, which is what to result means as a verb.

clue.text: Concerning journalist to acknowledge having gone behind

blocks.note: on means about or concerning
ed is short for editor
to own a fault is to admit it

explanation.surface: A reporter is worried about admitting they have fallen behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also reads as a crossword clue label, a wink from the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that trails by a single goal or point is said to be this, so it has gone behind.

clue.text: Send flower to support tense husband

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after the other

blocks.note: t is the grammar abbreviation for tense
h is the abbreviation for husband
a flower here is something that flows, and a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Sending flowers to cheer up a stressed husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower means a thing that flows, a classic crossword trick for a river. Send means delight, as in 'that music really sends me'. THRILL is a corner entry: a kick is a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone is dated slang for exciting or delighting them, the same as giving them a buzz.

clue.text: Tracks fugitives leaving area

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it is taken out

blocks.note: people who have fled
a is the abbreviation for area; it is removed

explanation.surface: A pursuer follows escapees as they flee a region.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracks looks like a verb, hunting the fugitives, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Runways are the long strips aircraft take off from, and also catwalks or ramps, kinds of track.

clue.text: First-class drink and gallons in the cask?

blocks.note: A is the top grade
a spirit
g is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Good liquor stored by the gallon in barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: spirits and wine mature while sitting in barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine and whisky are left to mature in wooden barrels, so anything resting there is growing older.

clue.text: Peacekeepers reflected obvious sort of power

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

blocks.note: UN peacekeeping forces belong to the United Nations
plain to see

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops thought hard about an evident kind of military might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected' suggests thinking things over, but it turns the peacekeepers round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is one source of electricity generation, as are wind and solar.

clue.text: Sample of burkha/kimono fabric

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from something larger, so the letters are lifted out of the text

blocks.note: the letters span the slash between the two garments

explanation.surface: A swatch of cloth used for traditional robes.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash between the garments hides the join, and the burkha spelling supplies the KH.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a sturdy dull-brown cotton or wool cloth, used for military uniforms.

clue.text: Fat starts to appear newly ubiquitous between gym and work

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only those opening letters are kept
something placed between two things is enclosed by them

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school gym lessons
the opening letters of the three words
toil is hard work

explanation.surface: Body fat is suddenly showing everywhere for someone squeezed between the gym and the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Fat is cooking fat, not body fat. PE is physical education, the British school name for gym lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundnut oil is a vegetable cooking oil, and oils are a kind of fat in cookery and nutrition.

clue.text: Criticise camera technique

blocks.note: first meaning: to slate a film or play in a review
second meaning: to swing a camera sideways across a scene

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from film, which makes them easy to read as one idea: a critic attacking the camerawork.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviewers slate a bad show this way, and a cameraman sweeps horizontally across a view with the same verb.

clue.text: Bit of wordplay means ignoring the leftmost edge

indicators.note: the leftmost letter of a written word is its first, and ignoring it drops it

blocks.note: a play on words
agency means the means or instrument by which something happens; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A crossword pun works by dropping the letter at the left edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leftmost edge' looks like one phrase, but edge is the definition. PUNGENCY is a corner entry: a sauce with kick has pungency.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungency is sharpness of taste or wit, and an edge is a sharp, biting quality.

clue.text: Flipping insect bite!

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the order runs backwards

blocks.note: a small biting fly

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at being bitten by a bug, with flipping as a mild British curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping reads as a mild oath, but it turns the insect round. TANG is a corner entry: a drink with a kick has tang.
explanation.definitionFit: Tang is a sharp flavour, and a sharp flavour is said to have bite.
